transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
I... I keep thinking everyone would be better off if I just weren’t here anymore. These thoughts about not wanting to wake up won't stop, and I just don't know what to do anymore.
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people do not, or feeling very strongly that others are trying to harm you or that you are worthless in a way that feels fixed and unshakeable?

It's hard to admit, but when I'm alone in the call room or driving, I hear my deceased father's voice telling me I failed him and that my patients will die because of me. I am also completely convinced that my absence caused his heart attack, and I feel like my colleagues and patients are silently blaming me and waiting for me to make a fatal mistake. I just feel like an absolute fraud who deserves to be punished for all of this.
Have you ever had a similar episode of depression before, lasting at least two weeks, where you felt this low or had thoughts like these?
No, I've never experienced anything like this before in my life. These feelings and thoughts only started after my father passed away last year. Before that, I was doing okay and managing fine.
Over the past two weeks, have you also had a depressed mood or lost interest/pleasure in things most of the day nearly every day?

Yes, and it's actually been going on for months now, not just the last two weeks. I've completely lost interest in things I used to love, like hiking, photography, and cooking, and everything just feels flat and pointless. Most days I just end up staring at the wall in my apartment or mindlessly scrolling through my phone.
Have you had any thoughts of actually acting on these suicidal thoughts, or made any plan to hurt yourself?

On my worst days, I catch myself picturing specific ways to end my life, like driving my car into a barrier on the highway. But I haven't actually made an active plan to carry it out, and I've never acted on those thoughts.
When you hear your father's voice or feel blamed by others, do you ever recognize that these experiences might not be real, or do they feel completely true to you?

Logically, I know it sounds completely irrational and that my dad would never say those things to me. But in the moment, it feels entirely real and the voice is as clear as day. I get genuinely convinced that everyone is blaming me and that I really am responsible.
Have these beliefs and the voice ever felt completely untrue to you even while they were happening, or do they always feel fully real in the moment?

In the moment, they always feel completely, terrifyingly real and convincing, and I can't shake them off. It's only on the rare days when my mood lifts slightly that the voice and those beliefs start to fade into the background. Otherwise, even though the logical side of me as a physician knows it's irrational, it feels entirely true when it's happening.
Have you ever had any previous episodes like this before, with a period of depression lasting at least two weeks, even if they were not as severe as this one?

No, I have never experienced any periods of depression in the past, even milder ones. This is the very first time in my life that I have ever felt this way. Before my father passed away, my mood was always stable.
Have you ever had a period of several days or longer when you felt unusually energized or euphoric, needed much less sleep, talked more than usual, or did impulsive things that were out of character?
No, I have never experienced anything like that. I have only ever felt deeply depressed, completely exhausted, and slowed down.
Have you had any other psychotic symptoms, such as hearing voices commenting on your actions, seeing things others cannot, or feeling that messages are being sent specifically to you?

No, I don't see things that aren't there, and the voice doesn't comment on my ongoing actions or send me special messages. It is strictly my father's voice when I'm alone, telling me I failed him and that my patients will die, along with that constant feeling that my colleagues and patients are silently blaming me. I haven't experienced any other symptoms like those you mentioned.
Do the voice and beliefs only happen when your depression is at its worst, or have they ever continued for at least two weeks even when your mood was not depressed?

No, they have never continued when my mood wasn't depressed; they only happen when I am in this deep depression. They only started after I sank into this state following my father's death, and on the rare days when my mood lifts slightly, the voice and beliefs fade away. They have never occurred outside of these dark periods.
Have the voice or the fixed beliefs ever continued for at least two weeks when your mood was not depressed, or do they only happen during the depressive episodes?

No, they only happen during these depressive episodes and have never continued when my mood wasn't depressed. They only started after I sank into this deep depression, and they fade away or disappear entirely on the rare days when my mood lifts even a little. They have never occurred during times when I was feeling okay.
